target: Komşumuz bugün gazete okudu ama pek beğenmedi.
english: Our neighbor read the newspaper today but didn't really like it.
tip: With a negative verb, ‘pek’ means not really rather than very: ‘pek beğenmedi’, did not really like it.

target: Ne çay istiyorum ne de kahve, su getirin.
english: I want neither tea nor coffee, bring water.
tip: ‘ne’ with ‘ne de’ means neither nor: ‘ne çay ne de kahve’, neither tea nor coffee, and the verb itself stays positive.

target: Komşu kadın kar yağarken çay ocağında çocuklarla oynuyordu.
english: The neighbor woman was playing with children at the tea shop while it was snowing.
tip: Add ‘-ken’ for while at the same time: ‘yağ’ (fall or snow) plus ‘arken’ gives ‘yağarken’, while it was snowing.

target: Bir yandan maaş iyi, öte yandan çalışma saatleri uzun.
english: On one hand the salary is good, on the other the hours are long.
tip: ‘bir yandan’ with ‘öte yandan’ sets up two sides: on one hand the pay, on the other hand the hours.

english: If we win we'll be champions.
tip: For a real, likely condition use aorist plus ‘-sa’: ‘kazan’ (win) plus ‘ır’ plus ‘sak’ gives ‘kazanırsak’, if we win.

english: I wish I had studied more.
tip: ‘keşke’ (if only) pairs with the ‘-saydı’ past to voice a regret: ‘keşke çalışsaydım’, I wish I had studied.

english: I brushed my teeth before going to bed.
tip: Verb plus ‘-madan önce’ means before doing: ‘yatmadan önce’, before going to bed, and the verb carries no tense.

english: When it snowed, I didn't want to go outside.
tip: Add ‘-dığında’ to a verb for when it happened: ‘yağdığında’, when it snowed.

target: Çocuklara kitap okuma alışkanlığı kazandırmak önemli.
english: It's important to instill reading habits in children.
tip: The causative ‘-dır’ makes someone gain something: ‘kazan’ (gain) plus ‘dır’ gives ‘kazandırmak’, to make gain or instill.

target: Yolculukta yanımıza yiyecek bir şeyler almayı unutmayalım.
english: Let's not forget to take something to eat with us on the trip.
tip: The ‘-alım’ ending makes a let us suggestion, here negative: ‘unutmayalım’, let us not forget.

target: Arkeologlar Hitit dönemine ait seramik tabletler bulmuş.
english: Archaeologists have found ceramic tablets from the Hittite period.
tip: ‘ait’ (belonging to) takes the dative on the word before it: ‘dönemine ait’, belonging to the period.

english: We must not miss this opportunity.
tip: ‘kaçırmamalıyız’ means must not miss. The ‘-malı’ is the must part, and the ‘-ma-’ right before it makes it negative.

english: Run as fast as you can.
tip: ‘koşabildiğin kadar’ means as fast as you can run. ‘-abil’ marks ability, and ‘kadar’ sets the as much as limit.

english: The food you cooked was very delicious.
tip: ‘pişirdiğin yemek’ means the food you cooked. The ‘-diğin’ ending makes a verb describe the noun right after it.

english: I must finish this report by tomorrow.
tip: ‘yarına kadar’ means by tomorrow. ‘kadar’ needs the dative ‘-a’ on the time word, giving ‘yarına’ from ‘yarın’.

english: We can go by car or we can walk.
tip: ‘arabayla’ means by car. The ‘-yla’ ending marks the means you use; the ‘y’ is just a buffer after the vowel.

english: This soup recipe was passed down from my grandmother.
tip: ‘babaannemden’ means from my grandmother. The ‘-den’ ending marks the source that something comes from.

english: Could you tell me where the bus stop is?
tip: ‘söyler misiniz’ is a polite request. The aorist ‘söyler’ plus the question ‘misiniz’ softens it to could you tell.

target: Yerinde olsam o teklifi kabul ederdim.
english: If I were you, I would accept that offer.
tip: ‘yerinde olsam’ sets an unreal if with ‘-sa’, and ‘ederdim’ answers it with the would ending ‘-erdi’.

target: Dedem geldiğinde yemek çoktan hazır olacak.
english: When my grandfather arrives the food will already be ready.
tip: ‘geldiğinde’ means when he arrives. The ‘-diğinde’ ending on a verb builds a when clause.

target: Biz akşamleyin film izledik ve eve döndük.
english: We watched a movie in the evening and went home.
tip: ‘akşamleyin’ means in the evening. The ‘-leyin’ ending turns a time word into an at that time adverb.

english: If I hadn't forgotten my umbrella, I wouldn't have got wet.
tip: ‘unutmasaydım’ means if I hadn't forgotten. The ‘-masaydı’ ending builds an unreal condition about the past.

english: We must wash our hands before eating.
tip: ‘önce’ meaning before takes the ablative ‘-ten’: ‘yemekten önce’ means before the meal.

english: When the storm hit, I put on my raincoat.
tip: ‘çıkınca’ means when it broke out, or as soon as it did. The ‘-ınca’ ending links one action right before another.

english: In the square very beautiful flowers have bloomed.
tip: ‘açmış’ uses ‘-mış’ for something noticed after the fact: the flowers have bloomed, going by what you see now.

english: According to the news it will rain tomorrow.
tip: ‘göre’ meaning according to takes the dative ‘-e’: ‘haberlere göre’ means according to the news.

target: Dün sabahtan beri hiçbir şey yemedim.
english: I haven't eaten anything since yesterday morning.
tip: ‘beri’ meaning since takes the ablative ‘-tan’: ‘sabahtan beri’ means since the morning.

target: Yaşlılara yardım etmeli ve saygılı olmalıyız.
english: We should help the elderly and be respectful.
tip: ‘yardım etmek’ takes the dative for who gets helped: ‘yaşlılara’ means to the elderly, with the dative ‘-a’ on ‘yaşlılar’.

target: Daha büyük bir daireye taşınmayı planlıyorlar.
english: They are planning to move to a bigger apartment.
tip: ‘taşınmayı’ turns the verb move into an object: ‘-ma’ makes it a noun, ‘-yı’ marks it as what they plan.

target: Banyodaki akan musluğu tamir etmemiz gerekiyor.
english: We need to fix the leaking tap in the bathroom.
tip: ‘tamir etmemiz gerekiyor’ means we need to fix it. ‘-memiz’ carries the we, and ‘gerekiyor’ adds the need.
